evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary records 𥉏 as a variant of 看. It quotes Shuowen’s 看 or from 倝, and says the later regularized form 𥉏 is the standard-form rendering of that Shuowen alternate. This supports describing the proposed direction 看’s alternate form → later regularized 𥉏, while leaving the date and path of the graphic change unspecified.

Its form tables show a Xiaozhuan example but no bronze, oracle-bone, or bamboo-and-silk record for 看. It cites transmitted examples for observe, regard, view, hear, guard, and an auxiliary use; these are examples for separate uses, not proof of a dated semantic chain.

gaps: No visual pixel inspection was performed in this research stage. The Commons description and provenance identify the asset as a Shuowen seal-style digital drawing; the harness or visual reviewer should inspect rendered pixels before final selection.
The exact Sinica 27.770B character page was not retrievable, so its label, dating details, and direct CC0 glyph asset could not be checked. Do not substitute a guessed Xiaoxuetang image URL.
No verified oracle-bone, bronze, or securely dated Warring States form for 看 was retrieved. Available form catalogues show/describe received Shuowen or seal-style forms, not an artifact chronology.

The Ministry of Education dictionary supports 𥉏 as a later regularized form of the Shuowen alternate from 倝. It does not date that regularization or establish a continuous graphic path or corruption sequence.

The Commons page states the exact direct SVG URL and licensing, but both the direct image open and exact imageinfo API request failed through the web tool; no API metadata beyond the inspected Commons description page was verified.

The direct Xiaoxuetang 看 record was not accessible, so no Sinica-sourced glyph is proposed. The exact Commons image itself could not be pixel-inspected with the available web tool.
